question: Which edit grouping and replay rules preserve user intent, and can competing history owners be removed?
trigger: User explicitly requested another Best API Review of history after the accepted replay, grouping, publication, mounted-runtime and Plate configuration plan was fully implemented and verified; assessment and review recording only.
requirements: Reassess all 10 history ledger units from current jobs and hard laws rather than treating the implemented plan as presumptively correct.

Preserve complete atomic replay, skipped and remote change mapping, effects, schema identity, exact selection and root ownership, native composition grouping, editor and view retirement, and authored conflict semantics.
Delete, merge, inline, move or replace each surviving public history surface, facade, lifecycle bridge and mounted adapter unless an independent current job earns it.
Distinguish ordinary lazy availability, explicit stack inspection, persistence and transaction-local grouping policy instead of inferring one job from another.
Issue one value verdict, account for every ledger unit, reconcile the September 15 Pursue record and keep adoption and proof state separate from this review.
evidenceReuse: Freshly traced the implemented public API, transaction guard/publication sequence, history state and codec owners, mounted replay and focus handoff, Plate descriptor configuration, toolbar controller, Yjs depth consumer and non-test policy callers. Reused the source-bound final production, grouping, publication, package and browser receipts recorded by the completed plan because their implementation identity and governing requirements remain current; no old failing diagnostic was treated as current behavior and no upstream discovery was needed.
summary: Stop further history redesign. Complete replay belongs in editor.api.history; transaction policy stays in editor.update/tx.history; lazy availability and explicit immutable stack inspection have separate current jobs; Plate configuration keeps one descriptor and recorder. Atomic history publication already uses the generic private transaction-guard hook, while the remaining history-specific core bridge carries only batch identity and replay receipts for mounted selection/focus repair. Deleting or generalizing any surviving owner moves work, adds methods or creates a lifecycle protocol without removing a current responsibility.
alternatives: Keep/configure: keep one Plite history owner with explicit undo/redo services, lazy hasUndo/hasRedo reads, opt-in immutable stack inspection, transaction-local policy and validated codecs. Keep Plate configuration in plugin initialState so one live descriptor and recorder consume the store.

Delete full stack inspection: rejected. A current Yjs collaboration example reads branch depths and the surface supports explicit immutable inspection; replacing it with depth-specific methods or History JSON would add API or conflate inspection with persistence while retaining the same internal branches.

Merge editor.update({ history }) with tx.history controls: rejected. Outer callers choose update policy before authoring, while nested helpers and plugin actions must select policy inside an update they do not own; both forms have current non-test consumers.

Add a generic transactional plugin-state participant: rejected. History already prepares through the private generic registerEditorTransactionGuard hook and publishes before observers. Extending one protocol across authored state, anchors, plugin configuration and mounted receipts would conflate distinct failure and lifetime laws.

Delete or generalize the history-specific core bridge: rejected. It carries private next-batch identity and applied-replay receipts across the optional model/React boundary so projected selection and focus follow the exact replay. There is no second consumer that earns a generic metadata registry.

Move replay or grouping to React, Plate or Yjs: rejected. Headless/raw Plite, Plate and collaboration share one document-local stack; native and UI layers only settle input, choose focus and decode events. A second clock or replay authority previously produced observable disagreement.

Merge the Plate and Plite history entrypoints: rejected. The Plite subpath owns optional raw installation and codecs; the Plate facade owns default plugin composition, live state configuration and Plate declarations without another history engine.

Replace inverse canonical batches with document snapshots, authored history or a Yjs UndoManager: rejected. Those replacements lose skipped/remote mapping, domain effects, root/selection identity, raw offline editing, or retained authored attribution and dependency semantics.
proofLimits: 10 expected/10 reviewed/0 excluded/0 unreviewed or disposition-unresolved ledger units. This reassessment is source and consumer analysis; it changed no product code and reran no product test. The adopted implementation retains verified ledger state from source-bound receipts: the complete production service packet reports 224/224 rows, grouping and publication packets pass, strict Plite/package/declaration/import and managed browser checks pass, and AI correctness plus numeric budgets pass. AI timing remains formally inconclusive under the frozen paired-noise rule, so no speed claim is made. Managed browsers do not prove physical-device IME behavior. No package publication or release is claimed. Stop rejects further redesign; it does not broaden those proof claims.
